findings.title: S3 Block Public Access configuration missing
findings.description: The bucket has no Block Public Access configuration, which defaults to public.
findings.recommendation: Enable S3 Block Public Access at both bucket and account level.

findings.title: S3 Block Public Access not fully enabled
findings.description: The bucket does not have all four Block Public Access settings enabled. This may allow public read/write access to objects.
findings.recommendation: Enable all Block Public Access settings on the bucket and at account level: BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets.

findings.title: IAM policy grants full admin (Action:* Resource:*)
findings.description: Policy 'DevOpsFullAccess' contains a statement that allows all actions on all resources. This is equivalent to AdministratorAccess.
findings.recommendation: Apply least privilege: grant only the specific actions and resources required. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate least-privilege policies.
findings.evidence: PolicyArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/DevOpsFullAccess, Statement Effect: Allow, Action: *, Resource: *

findings.title: CloudTrail is not enabled
findings.description: No CloudTrail trail found in this region. Without CloudTrail, API calls are not logged — incident response and forensics are impossible.
findings.recommendation: Enable CloudTrail with a multi-region trail. Send logs to an S3 bucket in a dedicated logging account. Enable log file validation.

findings.title: Security Group exposes SSH port 22 to the internet
findings.description: Security Group 'web-tier-sg' allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0. This is a common attack vector.
findings.recommendation: Restrict port 22 to specific trusted IPs or a bastion host CIDR. Consider using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager instead of SSH/RDP.

findings.title: S3 bucket encryption not enabled
findings.description: The bucket does not have default server-side encryption configured.
findings.recommendation: Enable default encryption using SSE-S3 (AES-256) or SSE-KMS. Prefer SSE-KMS for audit trail and key rotation capabilities.

findings.title: IAM user has no MFA device
findings.description: User 'deploy-user' has no MFA device configured. Without MFA, a compromised password gives full account access.
findings.recommendation: Enforce MFA via IAM policy (Condition: aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent). Use hardware MFA for privileged users.

findings.title: IAM user has no MFA device
findings.description: User 'ci-bot' has no MFA device configured. Without MFA, a compromised password gives full account access.
findings.recommendation: Enforce MFA via IAM policy (Condition: aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent). Use hardware MFA for privileged users.

findings.title: IAM access key not rotated in 143 days
findings.description: Access key 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE' for user 'deploy-user' is 143 days old. Keys older than 90 days violate rotation best practices.
findings.recommendation: Rotate access keys every 90 days. Use IAM roles instead of long-lived access keys where possible (EC2 instance profiles, Lambda execution roles).

findings.title: GuardDuty is not enabled
findings.description: GuardDuty is not enabled in this region. GuardDuty provides continuous threat detection using ML on CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs.
findings.recommendation: Enable GuardDuty in all regions. Use AWS Organizations to centrally enable GuardDuty across all accounts.

findings.title: S3 bucket versioning not enabled
findings.description: Versioning is not enabled. Without versioning, deleted or overwritten objects cannot be recovered — this increases ransomware impact.
findings.recommendation: Enable versioning on the bucket. Consider MFA Delete for critical buckets.
